member.name: T:IlUtils.IlUtil
member.summary: Hand-written IL utilities that cannot be expressed in C#.

remarks.para: Motivation. The BCL's System.Threading.Volatile provides volatile reads and writes only for specific primitive types and reference types. There is no generic overload for an unconstrained T because the C# compiler refuses to emit the volatile. ldobj/stobj !!T IL sequence when T is not constrained to a known-atomic type. This class fills that gap with hand-written IL for callers that need volatile access on a generic field where the concrete T is known to be safe at the call site (e.g. an int, long, IntPtr, or a pointer-sized struct wrapping a single primitive).

When to use. Generic infrastructure such as lock-free containers, thread-safe lazy wrappers, or source-generated code that must work with an arbitrary T supplied by the caller, where the caller guarantees the concrete type is pointer-sized and naturally aligned.

member.name: M:IlUtils.IlUtil.VolatileRead``1(``0@)
member.summary: Performs a volatile read of a value of type .

remarks.para: Emits volatile. ldobj !!T — an acquire-barrier load that the C# compiler cannot produce for an unconstrained generic. The barrier prevents the JIT and CPU from hoisting this read above a preceding store or from caching a stale value in a register across threads.

Atomicity warning. The volatile. prefix is a memory-ordering barrier, not an atomicity guarantee. The load is atomic only if fits in a single native-word read (i.e. sizeof(T) <= IntPtr.Size and is naturally aligned). For larger or misaligned types the hardware may split the load into multiple bus transactions, producing a torn read even with the barrier in place. For those cases use Interlocked, a lock, or a type specifically designed for large atomic access.

No compile-time guard. Unlike Interlocked, which exposes only safe overloads, this method accepts any . Passing a multi-word struct silently produces unsafe code with no warning. The caller is responsible for verifying that the concrete is pointer-sized and aligned.

member.name: M:IlUtils.IlUtil.VolatileWrite``1(``0@,``0)
member.summary: Performs a volatile write of a value of type .

remarks.para: Emits volatile. stobj !!T — a release-barrier store that the C# compiler cannot produce for an unconstrained generic. The barrier prevents the JIT and CPU from sinking this write below a subsequent load or from keeping the value in a register instead of flushing it to the coherence domain.

Atomicity warning. Same constraint as : the store is atomic only when is pointer-sized and naturally aligned. A larger can produce a torn write that is visible to another thread as a partial update, which may corrupt state in ways that are extremely difficult to diagnose.
No compile-time guard. The caller must ensure the concrete is safe. There is no constraint that enforces this at the call site.
